statement: For every degree d, Proposition 2.2 proves that the arithmetic action on the N_d rational curves is transitive outside a thin subset of rational configurations. Conjecture 1.5 predicts the full symmetric group S_(N_d); §3 proves this for d=3 (S12), while d=1,2 are trivial.

answer.text: Arithmetic group: trivial for d=1,2; S12 for d=3; transitive generally. S_(N_d) conjectured in this source.
answer.display: Arithmetic group: trivial for d=1,2; S12 for d=3; transitive generally. S_(N_d) conjectured in this source.
answer.qualification: Conjecture 1.5 is dated 2020 and is not asserted to be currently open. This is an arithmetic Galois statement, not an extracted geometric complex-monodromy classification.

source.location: Proposition 2.2, printed p.295 and following paragraph p.296; Conjecture 1.5, p.294; §3, pp.299–300
source.version: Published JTNB 32(1) (2020), 291–310; publisher PDF with cover page

scope: Arithmetic Galois action on degree-d rational plane curves through 3d−1 general Q-rational points; generic splitting field over the rational function field of the point-configuration space.
notes: The full symmetric-group statement is a conjecture in this 2020 source for general d. No current unresolved-status claim is made, and arithmetic Galois is distinguished from geometric complex monodromy.
